Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

agree verb

to a plan, on terms

also agreed!, come to an agreement, okay, OK

classical

Plaut. Capt. 378
Cic. Att. 6.1.14 (Lewis & Short)

convenit (inter nōs)

impersonal use of conveniō: mihi cum aliquō, or inter aliquōs; with ut and the subjunctive

it is agreed (between us); we agree on

Examples

  • Mē ad cēnam vocā. — Pol vērō vocō. — Eāmus intrō hinc. — Fīat.

    Invite me to dinner. — I certainly do. — Let’s go in, then. — Agreed.Ter. Ph. 1053–1054

  • Fīat, gerātur mōs tibi.

    All right, have it your way.Plaut. Asin. 40

  • Placet, pater lepidissime.

    Agreed, Dad, you’re the best.Ter. Ad. 911

Other words

  • Fīat. — Agreed! All right

    verb: present subjunctive of fīō, “let it be done” · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 1054; Plaut. Asin. 40; Traupman 110; Traupman 104, 353: O.K., fīat or licet

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.)

    The reply to a proposal: Eāmus intrō hinc. — Fīat.

  • placet — agreed, fine by me; placuit, it was agreed, I decided

    impersonal use of placeō · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 911: Placet, pater lepidissime.; Cic. de Or. 1.155: posteā mihi placuit, … ut summōrum ōrātōrum Graecās ōrātiōnēs explicārem

See also agree, suggest, of course.

SourcesLewis & Short: convenio · Lewis & Short: fio · Lewis & Short: placeo
